test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Sept, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is not correct about the Directive Principles of State Policy?

options.text: To ensure the above mentioned employment and clean working environment for men, women and children.
Providing adequate means of livelihood for both men and women
Ensuring equal remuneration for equal work only for men
Reorganizing the economic system to prevent the concentration of wealth in a few hands

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ensuring equal remuneration for equal work only for men**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** aim to **create a welfare state **in India.
 
• They provide guidelines to the central and state governments of India, to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• These principles are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to **ensure social and economic democracy**.
 
• Directive Principles advocate for equal pay for equal work for both men and women. Hence option 3 is not correct.
 
• Other options like ensuring employment, providing adequate means of livelihood, and preventing the concentration of wealth are aligned with the principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Directive Principles** are enshrined in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution, covering **Articles 36-51**.
 
• They are **non-justiciable** in nature, meaning they are **not enforceable by any court**, but the principles are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• These principles aim to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order in which justice, social, economic, and political, shall inform all institutions of national life.
 
• Examples of the Directive Principles include the provision for free legal aid, promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections, and separation of the judiciary from the executive.
